text: Heating the whey to 90 °C makes its proteins coagulate and rise as a thin skin, which is skimmed off and set aside as a cheese-like curd (urda); the whey left behind is poured into a wooden barrel, where the natural microflora of whey and barrel sour it over several days. This account is second-hand, from a summary of the żentyca papers.
